entry.title: Show HN: I Wrote FlightTrack Twice (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: FlightTrack was my iPhone flight tracker from the early App Store days (bestselling travel app for 4 years), and I just rewrote it from scratch. I first wrote FlightTrack as a side project in 2008. It did really well and I quit my day job and started a company around it that was bought by Expedia in 2010; Expedia retired the app in 2017. By then I had burned out and focused my energy on classical singing, which turns out to mean living in airports. But I missed the app. This summer I started rebuilding it from scratch, with a design inspired by Paul Mijksenaar's fantastic signage at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, and working with Claude to write a server in Go and an iOS app in Swift. In 2008 v1.0 took me 6 weeks of evenings/weekends; now it took about the same amount of time, but thanks to Claude, I ended up with much more functionality (e.g. inbound flight tracking) and was able to try entire design iterations as functional code rather than just mockups. The data is way more expensive now, so it's a $59.99/yr subscription, but I'm giving a free year to the first 100 subscribers. I'll be adding lots of features soon but wanted to get this version out for Thanksgiving travel. Let me know anything you want and I'll do my best! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50604007 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
